title: Client-orphaned-generation-sweep-and-dynamic-backpressure-thresholds
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We continue to see edge cases where client disconnects or aggressive timeouts leave partial generations orphaned in the serving layer and prefix/KV caches. These orphaned generations increase memory pressure and skew batching decisions, causing tail latency regressions for high-concurrency tenants. Objective: Implement a deterministic sweep + reclamation flow and add dynamic backpressure thresholds that adapt to observed client behaviors and workload to reduce waste and improve tail latency while preserving resume semantics for customer-integrated tooling (function calling, structured outputs).
acceptance_criteria: Orphaned partial generations are reclaimed automatically within configured TTL windows and do not exceed configured mem pressure budgets
Serving node mem usage from cacheable partial outputs reduced by >= 40% in synthetic repro scenario
Resume API still allows reconnection within TTL and recovers structured outputs (function call state) in >= 95% of reconnection attempts during tests
Dynamic backpressure adjusts batch windows/arrival thresholds and reduces 99th percentile latency by at least 10% for customer workload X
All changes covered by unit tests, integration tests, and a canary rollout with metrics dashboards
design_notes: We propose a two-tier reclamation scheme: (1) Soft sweep: mark stale generations for incremental eviction based on inactivity and recent KV cache usage patterns; (2) Hard sweep: fully purge generations when node-level memory pressure crosses configurable thresholds or global policy indicates reclaim. Backpressure tuning will be driven by a percentile-based sliding window on request arrival and generation length; thresholds will be adjusted by an autoscaler component that uses heuristics from recent tail latency and batch fill rates. Resume tokens will be persistently checkpointed to the prefix index (metadata only) so that short reconnects can rehydrate without retaining full generation buffers in memory. For function/tool call state, we will serialize minimal call graph checkpoints alongside the resume token to allow correct structured output reconstruction on resume.
implementation_steps: Spec: finalize TTL and memory-pressure thresholds and publish to runtime-configs (PRD link in related_links)
Runtime: add soft-sweep marker and per-generation last-active timestamp to prefix index
Runtime: implement hard-sweep trigger on mem-pressure with graceful preemption and fallback to shorter variants
Resume: checkpoint function-call metadata and structured-output fragments to prefix index with schema versioning
Backpressure: add sliding-window percentile sampler and controller that exposes thresholds via metrics and feature flags
Testing: build synthetic harness to emulate high connect/disconnect churn with tool-calling flows
Docs: update console runbooks and API docs for resume behavior and TTLs
Rollout: staged canary across 5%->25%->100% with playbook for rollback
testing_plan: Unit tests for marker lifecycle and checkpoint serialization. Integration tests: replay a recorded high-churn workload (tool-calling + structured outputs) and assert memory delta and resume success rates. Chaos tests: simulate node OOM triggers to verify hard-sweep correctness and downstream client experience. Canary: run against a shadowed production tenant for 48 hours while monitoring mem pressure, 99/999 latency, resume success, and error rates.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged rollout. Stage 1: internal canary on staging infra. Stage 2: 5% canary on non-critical production tenants with elevated observability. Stage 3: 25% spread across regions. Stage 4: global enable. If resume success drops below 90% or tail latency regresses >5% for >30m, rollback to previous config and engage oncall.
risks: Incorrect serialization of function-call checkpoints could lead to corrupted structured outputs on resume
Aggressive hard-sweep may drop resumable state too early for legitimately slow clients
Dynamic threshold controller could oscillate if poorly tuned, creating flapping behavior
Prefix index growth from checkpoint metadata if TTLs are misconfigured
